D1.defect: The loop-in where we wrote last can't be addressed to the current contact. The prompt says 'email_compose action reply on the thread's latest message ... To and Cc set explicitly', but MCP Emails email_compose schema: to is 'Send and forward only: a reply goes to the original sender'. When we wrote last, the latest message is Akshay's own (ad@ Sent), so the reply goes To ad@thepodium.in. That breaks OUTSIDE MAIL ('Akshay is never in To'), and the contact is reached only if the model puts them in Cc. The inbox replay found the same limit (replay1B: 'a reply cannot set to').
deciding_lines: zoya-one L50 / zoya-slow L62: 'email_compose action reply on the thread's latest message in Akshay's inbox ..., reply_all false, To and Cc set explicitly'
zoya-one L96 HARD RULES OUTSIDE MAIL: 'To is whoever's move it is ... Akshay is never in To'
zoya-one L49 THREADING itself notes 'MCP Emails' reply puts the thread's last sender in To'
D1.fix: For the loop-in use the same path as THREADING: MCP Emails draft action reply on ad@ (inbox cd37e47e), then draft update to=[contact], cc=[...] , read back, then draft send with idempotency_key loopin:<Message-ID>. Or limit email_compose reply to the case where their side wrote last (To = their sender is then right). SLOW changes too, so the pin moves again.

D2.defect: The skills these routines run still tell the model to use Gmail. ft-host-dossier Stage 0: 'Gmail: search for the guest's name, company, ... PR agency'. Its checklist: 'Drive and Gmail searched'. ft-guest-eval step 5: 'Mail (Gmail on ad@thepodium.in ...)'. MAILBOX only remaps 'a step below', and a skill's steps aren't below. While the Gmail connector is still attached, which it is until the CTO detaches it, a skill run can call it.
deciding_lines: dossiers/evals L4 MAILBOX: 'Where a step below says Gmail, use: ...'
D2.fix: Add to MAILBOX in both prompts: 'This holds inside every skill you run: where a skill says Gmail, use MCP Emails on ad@ as above; never load or call the Gmail connector.' Better still, update the skills too.

D3.defect: The batch MAILBOX recipe is behind inbox round 2. (a) include_folders is ['inbox','sent'] with no 'archive'. The email_read schema says 'IMAP covers INBOX only unless you name archive or sent folders', so any thread the inbox routine archived (RSVPs) or Akshay archived can't be seen: booking threads, PR replies, Gemini notes. Sweep 6c is limited to 'inbox folder' as well. The inbox round 2 recipe uses ['inbox','sent','archive']. (b) The thread recipe searches by subject words, then reads each message to test References/In-Reply-To. Replay1A found that action read returns no headers, and round 2 switched to email_read search with text = the Message-ID. (c) 'a Message-ID: email_read original' covers reading a Message-ID but gives no way to find a message by its Message-ID, which evals STEP 2a ('by its msgid:') and dossiers ('or msgid:') need. Round 2 maps that as search text = Message-ID.
deciding_lines: batch.py mailbox(): 'include_folders ["inbox", "sent"]'; '(found by email_read search on its subject words, each read with action read)'; 'a Message-ID: email_read original'
inbox.py L38-43 (round 2): archive folder; 'rfc822msgid: email_read search with text = the Message-ID'; THREAD by search text = Message-ID
D3.fix: Bring the batch MAILBOX in line with inbox round 2: archive added to the folders, THREAD by search text = Message-ID with original reads, and finding a message by Message-ID through search text. For sweep 6c, use the inbox and archive folders, not the inbox alone.

D4.defect: Stale forward wording around the new 6c contradicts it. HARD RULES still read 'Never send mail other than STEP 6c (billing forwards to Jaya)'. Inside 6c: 'Personal purchases ... are never forwarded', and 'Once per message, by Gmail message id ... before forwarding, skip the message if an Activity ... holds its message id ... also skip it if Sent has a forward to Jaya'. That gives a second dedupe key (a Gmail id, which no longer exists) beside the new Message-ID one. The REPORT still says 'billing docs forwarded to Jaya (vendor: what)'. A model can read HARD RULES as permission to forward, or report a forward that never happened.
deciding_lines: sweep L109 tail ('Once per message, by Gmail message id ...')
D4.fix: HARD RULES: 'Never send mail (decision 420); create drafts only in STEP 3d.' Reword the 6c tail as 'never listed', with the dedupe keyed by Message-ID only (older Activities holding a Gmail id are history). REPORT: 'billing docs listed for Jaya'.

D5.defect: The weekly billing row's dedupe breaks at the week boundary. The search looks back 4 days, but a Message-ID is only skipped if it is already on the current week's row ('billing:<YYYY-Www>'). Monday's run will list Thursday-to-Sunday mail a second time on the new week's row. It's also not said whether <YYYY-Www> is the run's week or the mail's week.
deciding_lines: sweep L109: 'since 4 days ago' ... 'Source ID "billing:<YYYY-Www>": one row a week ... a Message-ID already on it is skipped'
D5.fix: Key the week as the run's ISO week, and skip a Message-ID found on this week's or last week's billing: row.

D6.defect: Drafts made as replies can't take the To the prompt asks for. The calendar FT thank-you is 'draft: a reply on the latest thread with the guest or PR ... To: the guest and the main PR contact (Via)'. The MCP Emails draft schema says to is 'Not for reply: a reply draft goes to the original sender ... an update can change it afterwards'. MAILBOX offers 'action reply' and never mentions the follow-up update, so the draft lands addressed to the latest sender (possibly Zoya or Akshay) and Akshay may send it that way. Sweep 3d says only 'Create a draft in ad@ (MAILBOX)' and leaves reply vs create open. Separately, a pre-existing conflict (not from 420): SLOW (4) says the FT thank-you is 'a standalone new mail, never a reply on the PR thread', while calendar says reply first.
deciding_lines: calendar L4 MAILBOX 'A draft: MCP Emails draft (action reply on a thread's latest message, or create for a new mail)'
D6.fix: MAILBOX: 'a reply draft: draft reply, then draft update with to and cc as the step says, then draft_read to check'. Sweep 3d: 'draft create, a new mail'. Settle the FT thank-you form in one place, ideally a new mail as in SLOW.

D7.defect: A 'gmail:<thread id>' Source ID is resolved 'by the guest's or PR's address and the subject', but the id doesn't carry the subject. A PR address has many threads (one per pitched guest), and evals STEP 2a's fallback is 'by the guest's or PR's address' with nothing to tell them apart. WhatsApp 0d has no MAILBOX block, so it has no recipe for gmail: ids at all.
deciding_lines: MAILBOX: 'a Gmail id or a "gmail:<thread id>" Source ID: find that thread by the guest's or PR's address and the subject instead'
D7.fix: 'By the guest's address, else the PR's address plus the guest's name or company in subject or body; several matches: take the one whose dates fit the row's Activities, and say so in the report.' Add the same line to WhatsApp 0d.

D8.defect: This is a dependency, plus one soft spot. Zoya reads Rules for Zoya every run as the source for 'the loop-in'. Until the CTO updates that page, it still describes the terse follow-up from ad@. HARD RULES ('from ad@ you send only the loop-in') wins, but the we-wrote-last form '<first name>, adding @Zoya to coordinate <the ask in a few words>' can grow into the old follow-up (e.g. 'any update on the precall? adding @Zoya'). There is also no explicit 'a loop-in Activity already on this thread: send none' past the 24-hour idempotency window. Zoya being in Cc normally moves the thread into her inbox, which mitigates this.
deciding_lines: zoya-one L6 Rules for Zoya '(... the loop-in)'
D8.fix: Update Rules for Zoya before deploying. Cap <the ask in a few words> at about 6 words, with no question mark and no date. Add 'skip if a Zoya loop-in Activity exists on that thread'.
